hero.eyebrow: Since v1.11: a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux
hero.title: Manga chapters → reader‑ready CBZ & EPUB
hero.lede_one: Paste a link from MangaDex or {{count}} other supported site, pick your chapters, and get clean CBZ or EPUB files that open on your e-reader or in your favourite comic app.
hero.lede_other: Paste a link from MangaDex or any of {{count}} other supported sites, pick your chapters, and get clean CBZ or EPUB files that open on your e-reader or in your favourite comic app.

desktop.title: Everything the CLI does, in a window
desktop.lede: No terminal, no flags to remember. The same downloader, with a native window on Windows, macOS and Linux.
desktop.overviewAlt: The desktop app with a series loaded: its title and chapter list, with 24 chapters selected and the Options tab beside them.
desktop.pasteText: Paste a series URL and the app loads its title, cover and chapters straight away. No "load" button, no copying chapter links one by one.
desktop.pickText: Type a range such as 1-10,12,15-20, or click a chapter and Shift-click another to select everything in between.
desktop.chapterListAlt: The chapter list during a run: the selected chapters, locked while they download.
desktop.volumesText: Pack each volume into its own CBZ or EPUB. Chapters are grouped by the volumes the site lists, or you can set the groups yourself, such as 1-7/8-16.
desktop.volumesAlt: The chapter list grouped into volumes, each with its selected count.
desktop.languageText: When a series comes in several languages or from several scanlation groups, the app lists the ones it actually offers, so you pick from real options instead of guessing codes.
desktop.languageAlt: The language dropdown open, with Catalan selected.
desktop.watchText: Live progress for every chapter, with the files landing in the folder you picked through your system's own folder dialog. When the last one's done, so are you.
desktop.themeText: The app follows your system theme, so late-night reading sessions stay easy on the eyes.
desktop.finishedAlt: A finished run in the Activity panel: all twelve chapters saved to the output folder, with a button to open it.

downloads.title: All downloads
downloads.intro: Latest release on GitHub. Unsure which one? Most PCs are x64; Macs take the universal app.
downloads.foot: The builds aren't signed, so Windows and macOS warn you the first time. Here's how to get past it.

features.title: Made for reading, not fiddling
features.ereaderText: AVIF pages become JPEG automatically, so they don't show up blank on Kobo, KOReader or Calibre. WebP too, if you ask.
features.cbzText: One CBZ or EPUB per chapter, or plain image folders with --format raw when you'd rather do the packing yourself.
features.bundlesText: --bundle packs a whole arc into one file, with a folder per chapter inside it.
features.rangesText: Ask for 1,3,5-10 and get just those, so catching up means downloading only what's missing. Skip credit pages with --skip-pages.
features.cloudflareText: Sites that need JavaScript or sit behind Cloudflare run through your own Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge, which even ticks "Verify you are human" for you.
features.dockerText: A tiny image for plain sites, and a :browser one with Chromium and a virtual display for the rest.
features.languagesText: Pick a language with --language, or a scanlation group with --scanlator when a site hosts several versions.
features.namesText: Name files your way with a template like {{filenameTemplate}}. Clashing names get a version suffix, never an overwrite.

sites.lede: From big aggregators to small scanlation groups. Other sites built on the same platforms often work too, even when they aren't listed. If yours doesn't, open an issue.

faq.title: When things don't go to plan
faq.smartscreenA: That's SmartScreen. The app is only flagged because it isn't signed. Click More info, then Run anyway. Windows remembers your choice.
faq.gatekeeperA: Gatekeeper blocks unsigned apps the first time. Try to open it once and dismiss the warning, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security and click Open Anyway. Open it again and confirm. You only need to do this once, for the app and for the command line alike.
faq.exeA: That's the command line tool, which runs from a terminal. Use the PowerShell one-liner and run it from there, or get the desktop app if you'd rather click.
faq.paywallQ: The newest chapter downloads empty or is missing
faq.paywallA: Many sites keep their latest chapters behind a paywall, and the page often looks normal. Try a slightly older chapter to confirm that the site works.
faq.oldQ: Old chapters are missing, or a warning says the range starts before the first chapter
faq.oldA: Sites often delete old chapters. manga downloader can only download chapters that the site still lists.
faq.browserA: That's expected for sites tagged browser in the list. The window opens when the site shows a Cloudflare challenge or a captcha of its own, and you're told when it may need you. Checkboxes are clicked automatically, but some challenges need you to solve them yourself; the download carries on by itself afterwards. In the app, an alert says the browser needs you, with Show the browser window to bring the window to the front and Dismiss to hide the alert. To open the window from the start instead, use --browser-visible, or Show the browser window under Options › Advanced in the app.
faq.nobrowserA: Sites tagged browser need Google Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge installed in one of its usual places. To use another Chromium-based browser, set MANGA_DOWNLOADER_BROWSER to the full path of its executable (or a command on your PATH), for example MANGA_DOWNLOADER_BROWSER=/usr/bin/brave-browser. It works for the command line and the app alike; for the app, set it in the environment that starts it.
faq.ereaderQ: Pages don't show up on my e-reader
faq.ereaderA: The site probably serves WebP images. Download the chapters again with --convert-images avif,webp. In the app, tick WebP under Convert to JPEG.
faq.unsupportedA: Try it anyway: sites built on the same platforms as listed ones often work. If it doesn't, open an issue or send a pull request.
